items.stem: The study of the relationship between physical stimuli and the experiences they produce is called:
items.answer: psychophysics
items.markingKey: (d) psychophysics.
options: neuropsychology
psychometrics
psychoanalysis
psychophysics

items.stem: Distinguish between 'stimulus' and 'sensation'.
items.answer: Stimulus: a physical energy that produces a response in a sense organ. Sensation: the first contact of an organism with a stimulus through the sense organs, giving rise to basic experiences such as hot, cold or red.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'stimulus' (a physical energy that produces a response in a sense organ.) and 1 mark for 'sensation' (the first contact of an organism with a stimulus through the sense organs, giving rise to basic experiences such as hot, cold or red.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about stimuli, sense modalities and functional limitations of sense organs is correct?
items.answer: The human sense organs can receive only a certain range of stimuli.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: The kinesthetic system gives limb position; the vestibular system gives balance. It is the minimum value of a stimulus needed to notice it. Sense organs work only within certain limits of stimulation.
options: The absolute threshold is the difference between two stimuli.
The vestibular system tells us the position of our limbs.
The human sense organs can receive only a certain range of stimuli.
Human sense organs can detect stimuli of any strength.

items.stem:
Statement: We cannot hear the very high-pitched sounds that dogs can hear.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Each sense organ can receive stimuli only within a limited range.
items.markingKey: (c) Each sense organ can receive stimuli only within a limited range.
options: Monocular cues such as linear perspective and relative size work even in two-dimensional pictures.
The relationship between the physical properties of a stimulus and our experience of it can be measured through thresholds.
Each sense organ can receive stimuli only within a limited range.
Sense organs show adaptation to constant stimuli.

items.stem: Explain the functional limitations of sense organs with examples.
items.answer: Limited range of stimuli; thresholds – too weak not noticed, too strong harmful; adaptation; e.g. cannot hear ultrasound, see infrared.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Limited range of stimuli; thresholds – too weak not noticed, too strong harmful; adaptation; e.g. cannot hear ultrasound, see infrared.

items.stem: "Psychophysics studies thresholds." Examine this statement with reference to stimuli, sense modalities and functional limitations of sense organs.
items.answer: The statement is valid. The relationship between the physical properties of a stimulus and our experience of it can be measured through thresholds.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (the relationship between the physical properties of a stimulus and our experience of it can be measured through thresholds.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Stimuli that are too weak or too strong may not be noticed or may harm the sense organs. The human sense organs can receive only a certain range of stimuli. Besides the five external senses, there are internal senses such as the kinesthetic and vestibular systems. Sense organs work within certain limits, and these limits are called thresholds."
(i) Explain the term 'stimulus', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: We cannot hear the very high-pitched sounds that dogs can hear. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The vestibular system tells us the position of our limbs." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) A physical energy that produces a response in a sense organ. (ii) Each sense organ can receive stimuli only within a limited range. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: The kinesthetic system gives limb position; the vestibular system gives balance.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) A physical energy that produces a response in a sense organ. (ii) Each sense organ can receive stimuli only within a limited range. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: The kinesthetic system gives limb position; the vestibular system gives balance.

items.stem: Explain the nature and varieties of stimuli and the sense modalities that receive them.
items.answer: Stimulus as physical energy; light, sound, chemical, mechanical, temperature; external senses – eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin; internal senses – kinesthetic, vestibular; thresholds.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: Stimulus as physical energy; light, sound, chemical, mechanical, temperature; external senses – eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin; internal senses – kinesthetic, vestibular; thresholds.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? Broadbent's theory that a selective filter allows only one channel of information to pass on for further processing.
items.answer: filter theory
items.markingKey: (a) filter theory: Broadbent's theory that a selective filter allows only one channel of information to pass on for further processing.
options: filter theory
multimode theory
psychophysics
principle of closure

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about attentional processes:
I. Internal factors affecting selective attention include motives, interests and expectations.
II. Divided attention is possible when one of the tasks has become automatic through practice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about attentional processes is correct?
items.answer: Internal factors affecting selective attention include motives, interests and expectations.
items.markingKey: (a) The others are wrong: Divided attention is possible mainly when one task is automatic. They are internal factors; size, intensity and motion are external factors. Broadbent proposed the filter theory; Treisman proposed the filter-attenuation theory.
options: Internal factors affecting selective attention include motives, interests and expectations.
Treisman proposed the filter theory.
Motives and expectations are external factors in attention.
Divided attention is easy for any two new and difficult tasks.

items.stem:
Statement: Auditory stimuli are better at holding sustained attention than visual stimuli.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Sensory modality is one of the factors affecting sustained attention.
items.markingKey: (d) Sensory modality is one of the factors affecting sustained attention.
options: Motion, intensity and colour of stimuli capture attention.
Driving has become automatic through practice, so attention can be divided.
Each sense organ can receive stimuli only within a limited range.
Sensory modality is one of the factors affecting sustained attention.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. An experienced tailor stitches a shirt while chatting with a customer. Identify the attentional process illustrated.
items.answer: Divided attention.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: divided attention.

items.stem: Compare the filter theory, filter-attenuation theory and multimode theory of attention.
items.answer: Broadbent – single channel filter blocks others; Treisman – unattended messages attenuated, can still be processed; Johnston and Heinz – flexible, selection at different stages, more effort at later stages.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: Broadbent – single channel filter blocks others; Treisman – unattended messages attenuated, can still be processed; Johnston and Heinz – flexible, selection at different stages, more effort at later stages.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. In a noisy party, Neha hears her own name mentioned in a conversation across the room. Name the attentional process shown here and explain it briefly.
items.answer: Selective attention (filter-attenuation): unattended messages are weakened, not blocked, so important words such as one's name can still be noticed.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for naming it (selective attention (filter-attenuation)); 1 mark for the explanation (unattended messages are weakened, not blocked, so important words such as one's name can still be noticed).

items.stem: What is attention? Explain the factors affecting selective and sustained attention.
items.answer: Alertness, concentration, search; focus and fringe; span; selective – external and internal factors; sustained – modality, clarity, temporal and spatial uncertainty; divided attention.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Alertness, concentration, search; focus and fringe; span; selective – external and internal factors; sustained – modality, clarity, temporal and spatial uncertainty; divided attention.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on attentional processes and answer the questions that follow.
"Divided attention is possible when one of the tasks has become automatic through practice. The object at the centre of awareness is in focus, while objects at the edge are in the fringe. External factors affecting selective attention include size, intensity, motion, novelty and complexity of stimuli."
(i) The filter theory of attention was given by: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'multimode theory' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Experienced drivers can talk while driving. (2)
items.answer: (i) Broadbent (ii) The theory of Johnston and Heinz that attention is a flexible system that can select a message at different stages of processing. (iii) Driving has become automatic through practice, so attention can be divided.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Broadbent (ii) The theory of Johnston and Heinz that attention is a flexible system that can select a message at different stages of processing. (iii) Driving has become automatic through practice, so attention can be divided.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'divided attention' and 'sustained attention'.
items.answer: Divided attention: attending to two or more tasks at the same time, which is possible when one task is well practised. Sustained attention: the ability to maintain attention on an object or event for a long period of time, also called vigilance.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'divided attention' (attending to two or more tasks at the same time, which is possible when one task is well practised.) and 1 mark for 'sustained attention' (the ability to maintain attention on an object or event for a long period of time, also called vigilance.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.stem: Recognising a word by first identifying its letters is an example of:
items.answer: bottom-up processing
items.markingKey: (b) bottom-up processing.
options: constancy
bottom-up processing
top-down processing
closure

items.stem: Distinguish between 'principle of closure' and 'principle of continuity'.
items.answer: Principle of closure: the Gestalt principle that we tend to perceive incomplete figures as complete. Principle of continuity: the Gestalt principle that we tend to perceive objects as belonging together if they appear to form a continuous pattern.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'principle of closure' (the Gestalt principle that we tend to perceive incomplete figures as complete.) and 1 mark for 'principle of continuity' (the Gestalt principle that we tend to perceive objects as belonging together if they appear to form a continuous pattern.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
items.answer: Proximity – incomplete figures seen as complete
items.markingKey: (a) Proximity – incomplete figures seen as complete is wrong: Proximity goes with nearby objects grouped together.
options: Proximity – incomplete figures seen as complete
Similarity – objects of similar form grouped together
Continuity – objects forming a continuous pattern grouped together
Symmetry – symmetrical regions seen as a figure

items.stem: The following statement about perceptual processes and perceptual organisation is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Top-down processing starts from the parts to recognise the whole."
items.answer: Bottom-up processing starts from parts; top-down starts from the whole.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Bottom-up processing starts from parts; top-down starts from the whole.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Explain any three Gestalt principles of perceptual organisation with examples.
items.answer: Proximity; similarity; continuity; smallness; symmetry; surroundedness; closure (any three with examples).
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Proximity; similarity; continuity; smallness; symmetry; surroundedness; closure (any three with examples).

items.stem: "A dotted outline of a face is seen as a face." Examine this statement with reference to perceptual processes and perceptual organisation.
items.answer: The statement is valid. The principle of closure makes us perceive incomplete figures as complete.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (the principle of closure makes us perceive incomplete figures as complete.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: In the study of perceptual processes and perceptual organisation, the term 'principle of proximity' refers to:
items.answer: The Gestalt principle that objects close together are seen as belonging together
items.markingKey: (b) 'principle of proximity' means the Gestalt principle that objects close together are seen as belonging together.
options: Attention focused on a limited number of stimuli selected from a very large number
The Gestalt principle that objects close together are seen as belonging together
The process of selecting certain stimuli out of many and focusing on them, involving alertness, concentration and search

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about perceptual processes and perceptual organisation is correct?
items.answer: Perception is influenced by the perceiver's motivation, expectations, cognitive styles and cultural background.
items.markingKey: (a) The others are wrong: The figure has a definite shape; the ground is relatively formless. Gestalt psychology holds that the whole is more than the sum of its parts. Bottom-up processing starts from parts; top-down starts from the whole.

Top-down processing starts from the parts to recognise the whole.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.answer: Motion parallax – near objects seem to move faster than far ones
items.markingKey: (a) Motion parallax – near objects seem to move faster than far ones. Convergence – eyes turning inward for near objects; Retinal disparity – binocular cue from the two different retinal images; Interposition – an overlapping object seen as nearer are the correct pairs for the others.
options: Motion parallax – near objects seem to move faster than far ones
Interposition – eyes turning inward for near objects
Convergence – binocular cue from the two different retinal images

items.answer: Retinal disparity – an overlapping object seen as nearer

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about socio-cultural influences on perception is NOT correct?

(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: People from different cultures may interpret the same picture differently. (2)
items.answer: (i) size constancy for distant objects (ii) The effect of a person's ecology, culture and experiences on how stimuli are perceived and interpreted. (iii) Perception depends on past experience, culture and ecology.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) size constancy for distant objects (ii) The effect of a person's ecology, culture and experiences on how stimuli are perceived and interpreted. (iii) Perception depends on past experience, culture and ecology.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? The Gestalt principle that objects similar in form are seen as belonging together.
items.answer: principle of similarity
items.markingKey: (a) principle of similarity: the Gestalt principle that objects similar in form are seen as belonging together.
options: principle of similarity
attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder
phi phenomenon
sensory adaptation

items.stem:
Read the following statements about stimuli, sense modalities and functional limitations of sense organs:
I. Stimuli that are too weak or too strong may not be noticed or may harm the sense organs.
II. The vestibular system tells us the position of our limbs.
III. Human sense organs can detect stimuli of any strength.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is incorrect: The kinesthetic system gives limb position; the vestibular system gives balance. III is incorrect: Sense organs work only within certain limits of stimulation.
options: II only
All of them
I only
II and III only

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about perception of space, depth and distance; constancies and illusions:
I. The movement seen in films depends on the phi phenomenon.
II. Illusions are caused only by defects in the eyes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: Illusions are misperceptions that most people with normal vision experience.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem: Read the case and answer. Seeing a row of dots arranged in pairs, a child says there are pairs rather than single dots. Identify the Gestalt principle illustrated.
items.answer: Principle of proximity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: principle of proximity.

items.stem: In the study of stimuli, sense modalities and functional limitations of sense organs, the term 'sensory adaptation' refers to:
items.answer: The reduced sensitivity of a sense organ to a constant stimulus over time
items.markingKey: (d) 'sensory adaptation' means the reduced sensitivity of a sense organ to a constant stimulus over time.
options: The ability to maintain attention on an object or event for a long period of time, also called vigilance
A misperception of a stimulus that does not correspond to its physical characteristics
The difference between the images formed on the two retinas, which helps judge depth
The reduced sensitivity of a sense organ to a constant stimulus over time

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about attentional processes is NOT correct?
items.answer: Treisman proposed the filter theory.
items.markingKey: (d) It is incorrect. Broadbent proposed the filter theory; Treisman proposed the filter-attenuation theory.
options: Divided attention is possible when one of the tasks has become automatic through practice.
Internal factors affecting selective attention include motives, interests and expectations.
Factors affecting sustained attention include sensory modality, clarity of stimuli and temporal and spatial uncertainty.
Treisman proposed the filter theory.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. Children from a city of rectangular buildings are found to be more taken in by the Muller-Lyer illusion than children from a village of round huts. Name the explanation shown here and explain it briefly.
items.answer: Carpentered-world hypothesis: people raised among straight lines and right angles read angles as depth cues and are more susceptible to the illusion.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for naming it (carpentered-world hypothesis); 1 mark for the explanation (people raised among straight lines and right angles read angles as depth cues and are more susceptible to the illusion).

items.stem:
Match List I with List II and choose the correct option.
List I:
A. Nose
B. Eyes
C. Ears
D. Tongue
List II:
1. smell
2. hearing
3. taste
4. vision
items.markingKey: (c) Nose – smell; Eyes – vision; Ears – hearing; Tongue – taste.

items.stem: Name two external and two internal factors that affect selective attention.
items.answer: External – size, intensity, motion, novelty, colour, complexity; internal – motives, interests, expectations, set (two of each).
items.markingKey: 2 marks: External – size, intensity, motion, novelty, colour, complexity; internal – motives, interests, expectations, set (two of each).

items.stem: Read the case and answer. As a friend walks away down the corridor, Meena does not think he is getting smaller. Name the perceptual constancy shown here and explain it briefly.
items.answer: Size constancy: the perceived size stays the same despite a smaller retinal image with distance.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for naming it (size constancy); 1 mark for the explanation (the perceived size stays the same despite a smaller retinal image with distance).

items.stem:
Statement: A hungry person may see food in ambiguous pictures.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Motivation of the perceiver influences perception.
items.markingKey: (d) Motivation of the perceiver influences perception.
options: Top-down processing uses context and expectations to recognise the whole.
Each sense organ can receive stimuli only within a limited range.
The principle of closure makes us perceive incomplete figures as complete.
Motivation of the perceiver influences perception.

items.stem: What is meant by 'sustained attention' in the context of attentional processes?
items.answer: The ability to maintain attention on an object or event for a long period of time, also called vigilance.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: sustained attention correctly explained as the ability to maintain attention on an object or event for a long period of time, also called vigilance.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: We can read a sentence with a misspelt word without noticing it.
items.answer: Top-down processing uses context and expectations to recognise the whole.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Top-down processing uses context and expectations to recognise the whole. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem:
Statement: People from different cultures may interpret the same picture differently.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Perception depends on past experience, culture and ecology.
items.markingKey: (b) Perception depends on past experience, culture and ecology.
options: Motion, intensity and colour of stimuli capture attention.
Perception depends on past experience, culture and ecology.
They are used to interpreting angles and lines as cues to depth.
Sense organs show adaptation to constant stimuli.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on stimuli, sense modalities and functional limitations of sense organs and answer the questions that follow.
"Sense organs work within certain limits, and these limits are called thresholds. The human sense organs can receive only a certain range of stimuli. A stimulus must be within a certain range of intensity to be sensed."
(i) After a while, we stop noticing the smell in a room. This is called: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'stimulus' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: We stop noticing the feel of our clothes after some time. (2)
items.answer: (i) sensory adaptation (ii) A physical energy that produces a response in a sense organ. (iii) Sense organs show adaptation to constant stimuli.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) sensory adaptation (ii) A physical energy that produces a response in a sense organ. (iii) Sense organs show adaptation to constant stimuli.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: A friend walking away does not seem to shrink.
items.answer: Size constancy keeps the perceived size stable despite the smaller retinal image.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Size constancy keeps the perceived size stable despite the smaller retinal image. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem: The following statement about attentional processes is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Treisman proposed the filter theory."
items.answer: Broadbent proposed the filter theory; Treisman proposed the filter-attenuation theory.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Broadbent proposed the filter theory; Treisman proposed the filter-attenuation theory.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.
